prerequisites: Calculation, Design and Testing of Machines (596)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge of all destructive and non-destructive tests used in industry, and necessary for all product quality controls. Understand the variability of materials and testing processes. Relate the molecular structure and behavior of materials to their response in engineering applications.

syllabus_topics: Destructive testing: mechanical properties (static: hardness, tension, compression, flexure, buckling, and torsion; dynamic: impact resistance, fatigue, and wear).
Forming tests: bending, deep drawing, forging, shearing, punching, and welding.
Characteristic tests (thermal analysis, micrographic, macrographic, and metallographic tests).
Non-destructive testing: radiographic, ultrasonic, penetrant liquids, magnetic.

Deformation of materials: Introduction. Deformation mechanisms. Rolling: rolling concepts, percentage of cold work. Forging: forging concepts and tests. Deep drawing: deep drawing concepts and tests. Cutting: cutting concepts and tests. Bending: bending concepts, types of bending, quality index according to Tejmajer and tests.
Characteristic tests: Introduction. Composition tests. X-ray structure tests. Thermal analysis. Constitution tests: Metallographic.

Mechanical properties tests: Introduction. Mechanical properties of materials. Static hardness tests: Brinell method, Vickers method, Rockwell method, Knoop method, microhardness. Tensile tests. Compression tests. Buckling tests. Torsion tests. Static flexure tests. Impact resistance tests: Charpy and Izod. Wear tests. Fatigue: concept of fatigue, phases, and tests.

Non-destructive tests: Introduction. Radiographic tests: definition, concepts, and radiographic techniques. Ultrasonic tests: definition, concepts, and ultrasonic techniques. Magnetic particle tests: definition and procedure of magnetic particle testing. Liquid penetrant tests: definition and procedure of liquid penetrant testing.

Heat and thermochemical treatments: Introduction. Development of heat treatments. Classification of heat treatments. Annealing. Quenching. Tempering. Thermochemical treatments: generalities and classification.
Mechanical and thermomechanical treatments: Introduction. Cold mechanical treatments. Hot mechanical treatments. Thermomechanical treatments: Ausforming.

Surface treatments: Introduction. Metallization: metallization technique, applications, and advantages. Hard chromium plating: hard chromium plating technique, applications, and advantages. Porous chromium plating. Aluminum chromium plating. New surface treatment techniques.

New materials: Introduction. Advanced ceramic materials. New metallic materials. Advanced polymers. Magnetic materials today. Nanomaterials. Biomaterials. Materials for lasers. Energy and environment.
PRACTICES: Technological tests, destructive tests, non-destructive tests and heat treatment tests.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, at least 50% of the score must be obtained in the written test. If this critical evaluation criterion is not met, the total grade for the course will be 'FAIL'. The resulting score from the sum of all evaluation systems will be truncated to a maximum of 4.5 points.
